fullPassage: You've probably heard that it takes about ten thousand hours of practice to become an expert in anything — a musical instrument, a sport, chess, cooking, or a foreign language. The research by K. Anders Ericsson on this topic has been written about many times, and it was made even more famous when Malcolm Gladwell described it in his bestselling book Outliers. However, recently, a cohort of researchers reexamined the studies and research behind the 10K figure and said, quite dramatically, that the ten-thousand-hour rule was utter nonsense. Specifically, there is nothing particularly special about ten thousand hours, and while practice is clearly important to boost performance, other factors may play an even more important role. What are those other factors that get us to expert levels of performance? Pure innate talent? Intelligence? Luck of the draw? Perseverance? Hard work? Yes, it's all of that... and more. Age, experience, and environment all play a role. In other words, there's no one certain factor that can predict or ensure mastery or optimal performance of anything.

questions.passage: You've probably heard that it takes about ten thousand hours of practice to become an expert in anything — a musical instrument, a sport, chess, cooking, or a foreign language. The research by K. Anders Ericsson on this topic has been written about many times, and it was made even more famous when Malcolm Gladwell described it in his bestselling book Outliers. However, recently, a cohort of researchers reexamined the studies and research behind the 10K figure and said, quite dramatically, that the ten-thousand-hour rule was utter nonsense. Specifically, there is nothing particularly special about ten thousand hours, and while practice is clearly important to boost performance, other factors may play an even more important role. What are those other factors that get us to expert levels of performance? Pure innate talent? Intelligence? <u>Luck of the draw</u>? Perseverance? Hard work? Yes, it's all of that... and more. Age, experience, and environment all play a role. In other words, there's no one certain factor that can predict or ensure mastery or optimal performance of anything.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 Luck of the draw가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② 개인의 노력과 무관하게 타고나는 우연적 요소
det.analysis:
① 체계적인 훈련을 통해 얻는 행운: luck of the draw는 훈련과 무관한 운명적 운을 뜻하므로 부적절

② 개인의 노력과 무관하게 타고나는 우연적 요소: luck of the draw = 제비뽑기의 운 → 태어날 때 정해지는 우연적 요소 (유전, 환경 등) ←정답

③ 전략적 선택에 의한 성공 확률: 전략적 선택은 의도적 행위이므로 luck과 반대

④ 경쟁에서 승리하는 기술적 역량: draw를 그림/끌기로 오해한 해석, luck of the draw는 관용구
det.tip: Luck of the draw = 어쩔 수 없는 타고난 운
